newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: Slovak VSZ gains nudge SAX index up 1.65 pts.
newsitem.headline: Slovak VSZ gains nudge SAX index up 1.65 pts.

text.p: Leading Slovak shares closed mixed in quiet trading on the Bratislava Stock Exchange on Friday, with gains to steelmaker VSZ and engineering concern Povazske strojarne nudging the SAX index up 1.65 points.
"It was a very quiet day with small volumes and turnover," said Creditanstalt's Libor Briska.
VSZ closed 10 crowns up at 560 after peaking at 636 during trading on the trade of a 3,262 package. But Briska said the 560 crown closing price appeared to be a fair level for the issue.
Povazske strojarne gained 10 to close at 330, boosted by its recent capitalisation bond.

VUB bank lost one crown to close at 1,699 after announcing a net loss of 1.314 billion crowns for the first nine months of the year, mainly as a result of a decision to settle its risk assets. But the bank said it would still post a net profit this year, though lower that its 648.7 million crown net in 1995.
"The SAX was up today but with weak nine-month results being recorded by VUB and others, I expect it to remain flat or even down till the end of the year," Briska said.
Overall volume fell to 181,707 shares from 665,242 shares traded on Thursday. Turnover dropped to 79.90 million from 361.90 million on Thursday.
